problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}6y\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,x\le y\le 1-z},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $xz$-plane enclosed between the $x$-axis, the $z$-axis,  and the curve $z=1-x$ in the first quadrant.

activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type III Regions

feedback.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{x}^{3}}^{8}z\,dy]dA
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,0\le z\le 4}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{x}z\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}z[y]_{y={x}^{3}}^{y=8}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $z$ and then with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{4}z(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(8-{x}^{3})[{\int }_{0}^{4}z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(8-{x}^{3}){[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=4}\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8(8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{[8x-\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =8(16-4) \\  & =96\end{aligned}
$$
